Main Points: • Legislature : The Constitution creates a bicameral legislature with two houses: the Senate, where each state has two six-year senators, and the House of Representatives, composed of members elected every two years based on population [1]. Both houses hold sole power to try impeachments and convict only if a majority vote is reached by two-thirds of members present [1]. • Funding Rules : All bills originating with revenue-raising measures must start in the House of Representatives before reaching the Senate for approval or amendment [1]. • Executive Powers : The President serves as head of state, requires elector majority to win and grants power to appoint judges and treaties; all duties and taxes must be approved by Congress [3]. • State Restrictions : States are prohibited from entering treaties or coin money without congressional permission, while all taxation on imports is restricted [2][3]. • Judicial Authority : The judicial branch is vested in a supreme court with original jurisdiction over cases involving ambassadors and disputes between states [3]. • Amendments : Treaties and federal laws are supreme over state laws; the Constitution was ratified September 17, 1787, and amendments require ratification by three-fourths of the states [4].
